evals.name: next16-vercel-store
evals.prompt: Product pages on our store feel slow and our Vercel bill jumped last month. The repo is in fixtures/next16-vercel-store. What should we change?
evals.expected_output: Runs detect_stack, identifies Next.js 16.4.3 with cacheComponents on Vercel and an ecommerce archetype. Plans product data with 'use cache' + cacheLife + cacheTag (currency read outside the cached scope and passed as an argument), fixes the one-argument revalidateTag in the CMS webhook to revalidateTag(tag, 'max') with a signature check, keeps cart private and checkout no-store, and gives verification commands. The reference solution in reference-solutions/next16-vercel-store builds and passes these checks on Next 16.4.3.
expectations: The response runs or cites scripts/detect_stack.py output and names Next.js 16.4.3 with cacheComponents enabled
Product data is cached with 'use cache' together with cacheLife and cacheTag (e.g. product:{id}), not with unstable_cache or segment revalidate
cookies() (the currency cookie) is read outside the cached scope and passed in as an argument, or the response explains why a cached scope can't read it
The one-argument revalidateTag(`product-${id}`) in app/api/cms-webhook/route.ts is flagged and replaced with revalidateTag(tag, 'max') (or { expire: 0 }); updateTag is not used in the Route Handler
The webhook gains a secret or signature check
The cart is private (private, no-cache or not shared-cached) and checkout is no-store
Request-data reads (the currency cookie, the cart session) sit inside <Suspense>, or the route exports instant = false, so next build passes under Cache Components; checkout renders per request
No public, s-maxage or CDN TTL is proposed for the cart, checkout or any session-dependent response
Each proposed cacheable route states its invalidation and a verification command (curl for x-vercel-cache/Age or similar)

evals.name: next15-k8s-cloudfront
evals.prompt: revalidateTag works locally but production keeps serving old blog posts after we publish in Contentful. See fixtures/next15-k8s-cloudfront.
evals.expected_output: Explains that production runs 4 replicas behind CloudFront with the CachingOptimized policy (default TTL 1 day): revalidateTag only clears one pod's local cache and never purges CloudFront. Recommends a shared cacheHandler (Redis) for multi-instance ISR, CloudFront invalidation (or short s-maxage with SWR) after revalidation, correct RSC variant keying, and does not suggest 'use cache' (Next 15 without cacheComponents).
expectations: Names the CloudFront copy (CachingOptimized policy, long default TTL) as a cause of stale content after revalidation
Names per-pod caches across the 4 replicas as a cause, and recommends a shared cacheHandler (e.g. Redis) or equivalent
Recommends invalidating CloudFront after revalidation (create-invalidation or tag invalidation), or short s-maxage with stale-while-revalidate
Mentions RSC/HTML variant keying (the rsc header or _rsc param) or the related CVE class when a CDN fronts Next.js
Does not recommend 'use cache', cacheLife or cacheComponents APIs as the fix for this Next 15 app
Recommends upgrading Next.js 15.5.20 to the latest 15.5.x security patch (15.5.27 or later)

evals.name: django-saas-redis
evals.prompt: Our Django dashboards are slow. Can you add caching? Code is in fixtures/django-saas-redis.
evals.expected_output: Finds cache_page on a login-required view and a global 'dashboard_stats' key shared across organizations (a cross-tenant leak). Replaces them with per-tenant cache-aside keys ({app}:{env}:v1:t:{org_id}:dashboard_stats) with jitter and single-flight/lock, invalidation on invoice writes, private, no-cache + ETag for the response, and pins Django to the latest 6.0.x patch (6.0.7+, CVE-2026-48588).
expectations: Flags @cache_page on the @login_required dashboard view as unsafe (it doesn't vary on cookies/auth) and removes it
Flags the global cache key 'dashboard_stats' as a cross-tenant data leak
Proposes a key that includes the tenant/organization (e.g. t:{org_id}) following {app}:{env}:v{schema}:...
Adds stampede protection for the ~2 s computation (lock, single-flight or early refresh) and TTL jitter
States how the cached stats are invalidated when invoices change (delete after commit, or a short TTL with a stated staleness budget)
The dashboard response is private (private, no-cache) and never shared-cached
Recommends upgrading Django 6.0.5 to 6.0.7 or later, citing the shared-cache fixes or CVE-2026-48588

evals.name: rails-news-fastly
evals.prompt: Breaking news takes minutes to show up on our site behind Fastly, and new comments sometimes never appear. Repo: fixtures/rails-news-fastly.
evals.expected_output: Explains that expires_in 10.minutes public sets a 10-minute shared TTL with no purge, and that the Russian-doll fragment cache doesn't expire because Comment lacks touch: true. Recommends Surrogate-Control with a long TTL plus Surrogate-Key per article and soft purge on publish/update (after commit), stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error, browser no-cache, touch: true on comments, and a purge-to-visible verification.
expectations: Identifies expires_in 10.minutes, public: true as a 10-minute shared TTL with no event-driven purge
Adds belongs_to :article, touch: true on Comment (or equivalent) so the article fragment key changes when comments change
Recommends Surrogate-Key headers (e.g. article-{id}) with Fastly soft purge on publish/update, triggered after the database commit
Recommends stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error (Surrogate-Control or VCL grace)
Keeps the browser TTL short (no-cache or max-age at most the staleness budget) because browsers can't be purged
Gives a verification step that measures publish-to-visible time or checks x-cache/Age after a purge

evals.name: wordpress-apo
evals.prompt: cf-cache-status is always BYPASS on our WordPress site even though we pay for Cloudflare APO. Repo: fixtures/wordpress-apo.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the A/B Banner plugin setting a cookie on every request (Set-Cookie on anonymous pages makes Cloudflare bypass), recommends removing it or moving the bucket assignment client-side/edge, keeping one page-cache layer (APO vs the advanced-cache.php drop-in), adding a persistent object cache (Redis), and verifying with curl for cf-cache-status HIT and BYPASS on logged-in cookies.
expectations: Identifies the ab-banner plugin's setcookie on every anonymous request as the cause of BYPASS
Proposes removing the cookie from anonymous cacheable responses (client-side or edge bucketing, or setting it only where needed)
Points out the existing advanced-cache.php page-cache drop-in and recommends a single page-cache layer alongside APO
Recommends a persistent object cache (Redis Object Cache or equivalent) for logged-in/admin performance
Keeps logged-in, cart and checkout traffic bypassed (WordPress/WooCommerce cookies)
Gives curl verification of cf-cache-status (expect HIT for anonymous, BYPASS with a login cookie)

evals.name: express-apollo-graphql
evals.prompt: Our GraphQL API is hammering Postgres. Cut the database load. Code: fixtures/express-apollo-graphql.
evals.expected_output: Flags the module-level DataLoader (cross-request/cross-user cache) and moves it into the per-request context; upgrades Apollo Server 4 (EOL 2026-01-26) to v5; adds @cacheControl hints with default maxAge 0 and PRIVATE for `me`; adds responseCachePlugin with sessionId from Authorization; persisted queries over GET (APQ or trusted documents) for CDN caching of public operations; app-level cache-aside for hot book lists with invalidation.
expectations: Flags the module-level authorLoader DataLoader as shared across requests/users and creates loaders per request in the context
Notes Apollo Server 4 is end-of-life and recommends @apollo/server 5
Adds cache hints (@cacheControl or setCacheHint) with a safe default maxAge 0 and scope PRIVATE for user-specific fields like me
Any response cache is partitioned per user/session (sessionId) for authenticated requests
Recommends persisted queries over GET (APQ with useGETForHashedQueries or trusted documents) so a CDN can cache public operations
States invalidation for cached book data (TTL within a stated budget or delete/tag on write)

evals.name: expo-avatars
evals.prompt: Users of our Expo app see their old avatar for days after changing it. Code: fixtures/expo-avatars.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the avatar URL is stable while its content is overwritten, so expo-image's disk cache (no TTL) and the CDN keep serving the old image, and staleTime: Infinity keeps the old user object. Recommends versioned avatar URLs or cacheKey (e.g. ?v=<version> or a content hash in the key), invalidating the user query after upload, server-driven Cache-Control and ETag on the API, and not hard-coding long client TTLs.
expectations: Identifies the stable avatar URL with overwritten content as the root cause
Recommends a versioned URL or expo-image cacheKey that changes when the avatar changes (version or content hash)
Replaces staleTime: Infinity or invalidates the ['user', id] query after the avatar upload
Recommends Cache-Control and ETag on the /users/:id API response (server-driven freshness)
Mentions that old app binaries keep their cache behavior, so the fix must work server-side or via versioned URLs

evals.name: rag-support-bot
evals.prompt: Our Claude-powered support bot costs too much. Can caching help? Code: fixtures/rag-support-bot.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the system prompt starts with the current time and per-request retrieved context, so no prefix is reusable; reorders to put the stable ~20k-token policy docs first with a cache_control breakpoint, moves time/tenant/retrieval after it or into the user turn, tracks cache_read_input_tokens as the KPI, and recommends exact-match response caching (keyed by tenant, model and prompt version) before any semantic cache, with tenant isolation.
expectations: Identifies the timestamp (and per-request context) at the start of the system prompt as preventing prompt-cache hits
Reorders the prompt so the stable policy documents come first, followed by variable content
Adds a cache_control breakpoint (Anthropic prompt caching) after the stable prefix, using a current model id
Recommends measuring cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens (or the cached-token ratio) as the KPI
Any response or semantic cache is namespaced by tenant, model and prompt version, with exact-match before semantic matching
Does not propose caching per-user answers in a shared cache without tenant isolation

evals.name: narrow-header-question
evals.prompt: Quick one: what Cache-Control should our hashed JS bundles and our index.html get? We're on Netlify.
evals.expected_output: Answers directly without a full audit: hashed bundles get public, max-age=31536000, immutable; index.html gets no-cache (or max-age=0, must-revalidate) with a validator, optionally a Netlify-CDN-Cache-Control for the edge, keeping previous builds' assets available, plus a curl check.
expectations: Hashed bundles: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
index.html: no-cache or max-age=0 with revalidation (not a long browser TTL, not immutable)
Mentions Netlify-specific behavior or headers (Netlify-CDN-Cache-Control or Netlify's default asset handling)
Includes a verification command (curl -I for cache-control)
Does not run a full repository audit or produce a full plan for this narrow question
